instruction: Select all text in the document and make it bold.

parameters.window_name: 04 CHIN9505 EBook Purchasing info 2021 Jan.docx - LibreOffice Writer

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to use tabstops to split sentences (first 3 words left, rest right). Successfully navigated Format > Paragraph > Tabs dialog and set a right-aligned tab stop at 15cm. Failed when manually editing each line to insert tabs: text concatenation errors, partial completion, unintended formatting changes.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Writer menus (Format > Paragraph), open dialogs, select all text (Ctrl+A), use toolbar formatting options, type text, use keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+Home, Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Z)
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed at precise text manipulation: inserting tab characters mid-line caused text concatenation, undo didn't fully restore state, and manual line-by-line editing was error-prone. Only completed partial lines with some getting unintended bold/red formatting.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a two-step task: select all (Ctrl+A) then bold (Ctrl+B). Model demonstrated Ctrl+A in the trajectory, and bold is a single toolbar/keyboard action. Partial credit rewards even partial bold application.
metadata.explanation: Task requires selecting all text and applying bold formatting. Getter reads the docx and counts how many text runs are bold vs total. Metric returns the fraction of bold runs as partial credit (0.0 to 1.0).

scoring_breakdown.bold_fraction: 0.0-1.0 - Fraction of text runs that are bold (partial credit)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts bold state from docx by iterating all paragraphs/runs and counting bold vs total runs using python-docx
Postconfig properly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring fresh state
Metric provides correct partial credit scoring (bold_runs / total_runs), returning 1.0 when all text is bold
Coverage is complete: the single instruction requirement (all text bold) is fully verified
Minor issue: metric ignores the 'expected' parameter entirely - the {'all_bold': true} rule is never consulted, but the scoring logic still works correctly since 1.0 = all bold

Minor issue: run.bold is True (strict identity check) won't match inherited bold from paragraph styles (None), but Ctrl+B application sets run-level bold directly, so this is appropriate for this task
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using the 'expected' parameter in the metric to support configurable thresholds (e.g., expected['all_bold'] could gate whether 1.0 is required or partial credit is acceptable)
Consider also checking run.bold via the style hierarchy (run.bold or run.style.font.bold) to handle edge cases where bold is inherited from paragraph style
